title: Thread patchwork + quantified tradeoffs (feedback synthesis)
body:
Purpose:
Synthesize customer threads (Sept–Nov 2026) into a compact set of patch proposals where we attach quantified tradeoffs (latency, cost, correctness risk) so eng/product can triage quickly. This is intentionally terse — working notes for sync with Serving Runtime + Optimize next week.

Topline narrative:
- Many high-value customers report intermittent latency regressions at tail (95–99p) when conversations run >2.5k tokens, often correlated with KV cache misses following model variant fallbacks or autoscale events.
- Customers want: (A) explicit controls for cache TTL and eviction heuristics per-customer, (B) a per-route fallback policy that keeps latency predictable, and (C) better cost estimates for quantization/precision tradeoffs.
- Quick hypothesis: 60–75% of tail-blips are due to cold-kv + model swap overhead; remaining ~25–40% due to cross-host batch skew when autoscale triggers.

Raw signals and example quotes:
- "We saw a 2.1x latency spike on Friday during a long-run session — this killed our agent SLA" — fintech-customer-alpha
- "When we switch to ded-customer pool, responses are faster but cost doubles — need predictable knobs" — enterprise-b2b-ops
- "Quantized model cuts our token cost, but sometimes hallucinations increase on multi-turn prompts" — ecom-PM

Representative metrics (customer-provided + our traces):
- median latency (hosted): 140ms token-step for short contexts (<512).
- 95p latency: 820ms; 99p: 2.4s. When KV cold (post-eviction): 95p -> 1.6s, 99p -> 4.1s.
- estimated incremental cost of moving to a ded pool: +95–120% per-hour committed spend, throughput per-GPU up ~1.8x (customer reports).

Proposed request catalog (short descriptions + estimated cost/latency impact):
1) KV cache TTL + soft-eviction API (customer-configurable)
   - What: route-level TTL + policy (LRU / size-based / steady-state hold).
   - Why: allow customers with bursty long-run sessions to keep KV hot across bursts.
   - Estimated impact: reduces KV-cold tail by ~50–70% for affected customers (95p latency delta -0.6s).
   - Rough engineering effort: M (2–4w).
   - Risks: increased memory use; needs accounting in billing.

2) Model-variant sticky fallback policy (sticky-fallback, max-switch-rate)
   - What: prevent frequent model swaps for a given session; allow config to prefer slightly cheaper variant unless error rate rises above threshold.
   - Why: swaps trigger cold-kv + kernel reorder overhead; sticky reduces swaps and tail latency.
   - Estimated impact: cut swap-induced tail events by ~80% in observed patterns; cost delta small (depends on variant).
   - Effort: M (3w).
   - Notes: requires metric hooks to detect degraded quality and automatic rollback.

3) Per-route cost estimator and rollout-sim (console + API)
   - What: show token-cost projections for batch/cold/hot KV and quantization profile impacts (2-bit/4-bit/FP16).
   - Why: customers repeatedly asked for clearer cost transparency before committing to Dedicated or Private.
   - Estimated impact: reduces procurement friction; enables better conversation about tradeoffs in sales.
   - Effort: S–M (1–3w for prototype).

4) Quantization safety profile per workload (evaluation harness)
   - What: auto-run small eval sets (client-provided prompts) to surface quality deltas and a risk score when changing quantization/precision.
   - Why: customers fear quality regressions; want guardrails.
   - Estimated impact: lowers adoption friction for 4-bit/2-bit quantized models, could increase adoption by ~15% for cost-sensitive customers.
   - Effort: M (3–5w), cross-team with Research.

5) Cost-anchored rollout playbooks (quick patches)
   - What: small set of engineering patches we can apply with low risk to reduce tail cost: prefix caching suggestions, per-route batching limits, tiny kernel-timeout tweaks.
   - Why: immediate wins while building larger features above.
   - Estimated impact: 10–25% immediate token-cost reduction for certain workloads; tail latency improvement 10–30%.
   - Effort: XS–S (1–2w).

Prioritization (proposal for triage):
- P0 (urgent for 3 enterprise customers): 1) KV TTL API, 2) Model-variant sticky fallback. (Why: direct SLA hits; customers asking for config knobs.)
- P1: Cost estimator + rollout-sim; short-term patches.
- P2: Quantization safety harness; broader, needs research support.

Customer impact mapping (quick):
- fintech-customer-alpha: P0 for TTL + sticky fallback; also asked for per-session billing visibility.
- ecom-PM: wants quantization safety first (P1->P2 depending on experiment).
- enterprise-b2b-ops: willing to sign Dedicated if we surface cost delta and provide sticky-fallback SLA.

Open questions we must answer before engineering kickoff:
- How will KV TTL interact with autoscaler eviction policies? (SRE input needed)
- Billing: do we implement memory-based surcharge, or attribute to request-level billing?
- Can we prototype sticky-fallback purely in the routing layer, or are deeper runtime hooks required?
- What metrics and SLIs should auto-trigger rollback for quantization (precision/recall thresholds)?

Quick experiment ideas (2-week spikes):
- Run synthetic long conversations with controlled KV misses (A/B): enable a per-route soft-hold (emulate TTL) for a subset of tenant traffic; measure 95/99p.
- Implement a routing-layer sticky flag on a small customer and observe swap-rate + tail-latency change.
- Add a single dashboard widget in Console that shows forecasted token-cost under current model variant and a 4-bit alternative (prototype using sampled telemetry).

Decision recommendations for the sync:
- Approve 2-week spike funding for the A/B experiments (SRE + serving-runtime + product). Owner: Maya Chen (CS) + Samir Gupta (eng-hosted).
- Engineering to scope KV TTL as a configurable router/runtime flag (not billing yet). If 2-week spike shows meaningful tail reduction, scope billing treatment in Q1 planning.
- Research to allocate 0.25 FTE for initial quantization safety harness design.

Next steps and owners:
- Schedule triage sync (30m) with Serving Runtime, SRE, Optimize: proposed 2026-11-23. Owner: Maya Chen.
- Create JIRA spike: RED-QUANT-TTL-01 (owner: Samir).
- Prototype routing sticky flag in canary: RED-ROUTE-479 (owner: Luca).

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Week 0–2: experiments + dashboards prototype.
- Week 3–6: small patch rollouts for KV TTL toggles + sticky fallback pilot for 2 customers.
- Q1 2027: billing model + quantization safety full rollouts if experiments validate.

Appendix (raw snippets / traces pasted from customer logs):
- Customer alpha trace (anonymized): session-id XYZ: large convo -> autoscale up -> model swap to variant-b -> kernel init 420ms + kv-warm 1.1s -> observed 99p 4.1s.
- Quick contact list: CS rep Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai), Solutions eng Luca Moreno (luca@redwood.ai), Research lead Priya Patel (priya@redwood.ai).

Unresolved small tasks:
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers already have any TTL/eviction controls in Private deployments (Priya to check).
- Collect 5–7 representative prompt sets for quantization evals from ecom and content-mgmt customers (action: Maya).

End of notes.

-- Maya
(working draft, do not publish as final)
